Written from origin develop `207716440e2a6282b90ed2a118614d9cf98bee1e` (measured by `git ls-remote origin develop` at 11:45 AEST 2026-09-18).
`Blockchain/Dev/scripts/smoke-test.sh` read at that tip: blob `d5d34357a0e4dd36d1ed951367a9ee189a337214`, **395 lines** (`wc -l`). Read line by line: `:1-146` (header, target, helpers, sections 1-3 and the `--quick` switch) and `:370-395` (the verdict). `Blockchain/Dev/deployment/azure/RUNBOOK.md:139-150` (section 2.2) read for the contract.

## THE MODE — read this twice

**BASH_PATCH.** Your diff contains EXACTLY TWO files:
1. `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/smoke-test.sh` — ONE hunk, a pure insertion (no `-` line).
2. `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/smoke_test_honours_smoke_base_url.test.sh` — ONE NEW file (`--- /dev/null`).

**In THIS tier the paths are FULL repository paths, `Blockchain/Dev/...`** — the checker applies with `git apply -p1` from the repository root. Nothing else changes: not the RUNBOOK, not the reference suite.

## What is wrong (one paragraph)

`RUNBOOK.md` section 2.2 tells an operator to smoke-test an environment with `SMOKE_BASE_URL=https://<prod-gateway-fqdn> ../../scripts/smoke-test.sh`. `smoke-test.sh:15` hardcodes `GATEWAY="http://localhost:6882"` and never reads `SMOKE_BASE_URL` (the name occurs nowhere in the script), so that run checks localhost while the operator believes it checked the named environment — a smoke pass that looks like it covered somewhere it did not. Found by the #1037 gate (O-2). **This task takes the ticket's first option: the script honours `SMOKE_BASE_URL` for its gateway target, with `http://localhost:6882` staying the default, and prints the target it is checking.** (The other option, "correct the runbook", is a docs edit with no tier here.)

## WHY THE TEST CALLS THE CODE DIRECTLY

The test runs `smoke-test.sh` itself — the script is its own entry point — with `curl` stubbed onto `PATH` (the `stack_guard.test.sh` pattern, which stubs `docker` the same way). The stub writes every URL it is handed to a log and exits 7, so no request leaves the machine. `--quick` mode stops after section 3, and every request in sections 1-3 is built from `$GATEWAY` (`:100`, `:128-133`, `:138-139`): exactly 9 URLs. No stack, no network, no Docker.

## Where (no `-` lines — every line below STAYS)

- `:15` — (correct) `GATEWAY="http://localhost:6882"` — stays as the DEFAULT; your insertion goes immediately AFTER it.
- `:16` — (correct) `RED='\033[0;31m'` — the trailing context line. Stays. Copy it byte for byte, backslash included.
- `:100` — (correct) `DEEP_RESP=$(curl -s -m 10 "$GATEWAY/health/deep" 2>/dev/null) || DEEP_RESP=""` — the first request; it reads `$GATEWAY`, so it follows the new value with no change. Stays.
- `:141` — (correct) `if [ "${1:-}" = "--quick" ]; then` — the quick-mode switch the test relies on. Stays.

## The exact change — ONE hunk in `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/smoke-test.sh`

A pure insertion between `:15` and `:16`: one context line above, your four `+` lines, one context line below. **Neither context line is blank** (line 14, above `:15`, is blank — it is NOT in the hunk). The `+` lines are ASCII only.

```
@@ -15,2 +15,6 @@

+# KS-1250: RUNBOOK section 2.2 points this script at an environment with SMOKE_BASE_URL. Honour it,
+# and say which target is being checked, so a run cannot look like it checked somewhere it did not.

Why this shape, so you do not "improve" it:
- `:15` is NOT removed. It stays the default and the new line reads it back: `${SMOKE_BASE_URL:-$GATEWAY}`. That keeps the hunk a pure insertion (no `-` line to get wrong) and keeps every run without the variable byte-for-byte as before.
- The `echo` is the ticket's "(and print the target it's using)". It prints BEFORE any check, so the first line of every run names the target.
- The comment says `section 2.2`, not the section sign: the `+` lines must be ASCII.

## The test — CREATE THE NEW FILE

File: `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/smoke_test_honours_smoke_base_url.test.sh`

**Reference suite (READ-ONLY, do not modify, do not add it to your diff):** `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/stack_guard.test.sh` (blob `07be45f99`). It locates its script from `${BASH_SOURCE[0]}`, stubs a command onto `PATH` with a heredoc, drives the REAL script, and ends by printing the totals and exiting non-zero on any failure — the shape below. It does not mock the script under test.

Write EXACTLY this file — two cells: one CONTROL, then one 🔴. It is bash 3.2: no `mapfile`, no `declare -A`, no `timeout`.

```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# TESTS for scripts/smoke-test.sh honouring SMOKE_BASE_URL (KS-1250)
# =============================================================================
# deployment/azure/RUNBOOK.md section 2.2 runs the smoke test against an
# environment with `SMOKE_BASE_URL=https://<gateway> ../../scripts/smoke-test.sh`.
# The script hardcoded http://localhost:6882 and never read the variable, so a
# run that looked like it checked that environment checked localhost instead.
#
# `curl` is stubbed onto PATH (the stack_guard.test.sh pattern): the stub writes
# every URL it is handed to a log and fails, so no request leaves this machine.
# The script runs in --quick mode, whose every request goes to the gateway.
#
# Usage: bash Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/smoke_test_honours_smoke_base_url.test.sh
# =============================================================================

set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)/smoke-test.sh"
PASS=0
FAIL=0

expect() {
  local desc="$1" want="$2" got="$3"
  if [[ "$got" == "$want" ]]; then
    PASS=$((PASS + 1)); printf 'ok   %s\n' "$desc"
  else
    FAIL=$((FAIL + 1)); printf 'FAIL %s\n       want "%s", got "%s"\n' "$desc" "$want" "$got"
  fi
}

tmp="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ks1250-smoke.XXXXXX")"
trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT INT TERM
mkdir -p "$tmp/bin"
cat > "$tmp/bin/curl" <<'STUB'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
for a in "$@"; do
  case "$a" in
    http://*|https://*) printf '%s\n' "$a" >> "$CURL_LOG" ;;
  esac
done
exit 7
STUB
chmod +x "$tmp/bin/curl"

# run_smoke <SMOKE_BASE_URL or the word UNSET>: runs the script in --quick mode and
# leaves the URLs it requested in $tmp/urls.txt and its output in $tmp/out.txt.
run_smoke() {
  : > "$tmp/urls.txt"
  if [ "$1" = "UNSET" ]; then
    env -u SMOKE_BASE_URL PATH="$tmp/bin:$PATH" CURL_LOG="$tmp/urls.txt" bash "$SCRIPT" --quick > "$tmp/out.txt" 2>&1
  else
    env SMOKE_BASE_URL="$1" PATH="$tmp/bin:$PATH" CURL_LOG="$tmp/urls.txt" bash "$SCRIPT" --quick > "$tmp/out.txt" 2>&1
  fi
}

# How many requested URLs there were, and how many of them start with $1.
url_counts() {
  local total under
  total=$(grep -c . "$tmp/urls.txt")
  under=$(grep -c -F -- "$1" "$tmp/urls.txt")
  printf '%s %s' "$total" "$under"
}

run_smoke UNSET
expect "CONTROL without SMOKE_BASE_URL all 9 quick-mode requests go to http://localhost:6882" "9 9" "$(url_counts 'http://localhost:6882/')"

run_smoke "http://smoke-target.ks1250.invalid:7"
expect "🔴 with SMOKE_BASE_URL set all 9 quick-mode requests go to that target, none to localhost, and the run names its target" "9 9 0 yes" \
  "$(url_counts 'http://smoke-target.ks1250.invalid:7/') $(grep -c -F 'localhost' "$tmp/urls.txt") $(grep -q -F 'Smoke target: http://smoke-target.ks1250.invalid:7' "$tmp/out.txt" && echo yes || echo no)"

echo ""
echo "smoke_test_honours_smoke_base_url: $PASS passed, $FAIL failed"
[ "$FAIL" -eq 0 ]
```

### READ THIS BEFORE YOU WRITE THE FILE

- The stub is written with a QUOTED heredoc (`<<'STUB'`) so `$@`, `$a` and `$CURL_LOG` are written literally and expand when the stub runs. Keep the quotes.
- The script's own output goes to `$tmp/out.txt`, never to the suite's stdout. Keep it that way: the checker reads this suite's stdout, and the smoke test's own `✗` lines must not be mistaken for the suite's.
- `env -u SMOKE_BASE_URL` in the control is deliberate: an operator's shell that already exports the variable must not turn the control into the red case.

## THE RED-FIRST CELL — state it to yourself before you write a line

**At the untouched tip, `🔴 with SMOKE_BASE_URL set …` MUST FAIL, by assertion.** The script never reads the variable, so all 9 quick-mode requests still go to `http://localhost:6882` and nothing prints a target: the cell reads `9 0 9 no` against `9 9 0 yes`. After your insertion, `$GATEWAY` is the `SMOKE_BASE_URL` value, all 9 requests go there, none to localhost, and the first line is `Smoke target: http://smoke-target.ks1250.invalid:7` — GREEN.

**MEASURED, not predicted** (Wednesday 12:0x, macOS `/bin/bash` 3.2.57, the tip's `smoke-test.sh` byte-for-byte in a scratch directory outside any repository): this exact test at the tip read `1 passed, 1 failed`, rc 1, the failure being the 🔴 cell (`want "9 9 0 yes", got "9 0 9 no"`). The hunk above applied with `patch -p1 -F0` (zero fuzz), `bash -n` passed, and the same test read `2 passed, 0 failed`, rc 0. (A first draft that REPLACED `:15` had no leading context — line 14 is blank — and BSD `patch` refused it; that is why this hunk keeps `:15` and inserts after it.)

The CONTROL is green on BOTH trees and stops a fix that breaks the default: without the variable, all 9 requests must still go to `http://localhost:6882`. A fix that hardcoded some other target, or that emptied `$GATEWAY` when the variable is unset, goes red here.

## Red cells

- 🔴 with SMOKE_BASE_URL set all 9 quick-mode requests go to that target, none to localhost, and the run names its target

## Output

Exactly ONE ```diff block, nothing outside it, with TWO sections in this order:
1. `--- a/Blockchain/Dev/scripts/smoke-test.sh` / `+++ b/Blockchain/Dev/scripts/smoke-test.sh`, ONE hunk `@@ -15,2 +15,6 @@` — context `:15`, **4** `+` lines, context `:16`.
2. `--- /dev/null` / `+++ b/Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/smoke_test_honours_smoke_base_url.test.sh`, ONE hunk `@@ -0,0 +1,N @@` where N is the number of lines you emit, every line a `+`.

- **P2 the file at the tip.** `smoke-test.sh` blob `d5d34357a`, 395 lines. `SMOKE_BASE_URL` occurs 0 times in it and once in the repo (`RUNBOOK.md:142`), searched. `:14` is blank; `:15` and `:16` are not.

- **P4 no sibling suite.** No `*.test.sh` in the repository names `smoke-test.sh` (searched), so the checker's B6 has nothing to compare.

## Notes for the raise (not for the model) — READ BEFORE RAISING

- **This is the ticket's first option, chosen by Wednesday, and it has a production consequence Kam should see before it is raised.** Today the RUNBOOK section 2.2 command silently checks LOCALHOST. After this change it checks the environment it names — and a FULL (non-`--quick`) run, which is what section 2.2 shows, then does what the script does against that gateway: sections 4-6 log in with the demo credentials, POST a `Smoke-Test` document and try to anchor it (`:147-214`). That is presumably what the runbook always intended for a post-deploy smoke, but until now nobody could have been doing it. **Queueing the brief is safe** (the harness only ever talks to its stub); **the raise should say this in the PR, and Kam should nod before it merges.**

Against a remote target those legs report unreachable. That is a separate decision (drop them in remote mode, or route them through the gateway) and is not in this diff.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# SECUURA PLATFORM — SMOKE TEST
# =============================================================================
# Verifies all services, APIs, and frontend portals are operational.
# Run after: container restart, code deploy, or any infrastructure change.
#
# Usage:
#   ./scripts/smoke-test.sh           # Full test
#   ./scripts/smoke-test.sh --quick   # Health checks only (no API tests)
# =============================================================================

set -euo pipefail

GATEWAY="http://localhost:6882"
RED='\033[0;31m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
CYAN='\033[0;36m'
NC='\033[0m'

PASS=0
FAIL=0
WARN=0
FAILURES=()

pass() { ((PASS++)); printf "  ${GREEN}✓${NC} %s\n" "$1"; }
fail() { ((FAIL++)); FAILURES+=("$1"); printf "  ${RED}✗${NC} %s\n" "$1"; }
warn() { ((WARN++)); printf "  ${YELLOW}!${NC} %s\n" "$1"; }
section() { printf "\n${CYAN}━━━ %s ━━━${NC}\n" "$1"; }

check_health() {
  local name="$1" url="$2"
  local resp
  resp=$(curl -s -m 5 "$url" 2>/dev/null) || { fail "$name — unreachable"; return; }
  if echo "$resp" | python3 -c "import sys,json;d=json.load(sys.stdin);exit(0 if d.get('status') in ('healthy','ok') else 1)" 2>/dev/null; then
    pass "$name"
  else
    fail "$name — unhealthy response"
  fi
}

check_http() {
  local name="$1" url="$2" expected="${3:-200}"
  local code
  code=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -m 5 "$url" 2>/dev/null) || { fail "$name — connection refused"; return; }
  if [ "$code" = "$expected" ]; then
    pass "$name (HTTP $code)"
  else
    fail "$name — expected HTTP $expected, got $code"
  fi
}

check_api() {
  local name="$1" method="$2" url="$3" data="${4:-}" expected="${5:-}" auth="${6:-}"
  local resp code auth_header=""
  [ -n "$auth" ] && auth_header="-H \"Authorization: Bearer $auth\""
  if [ "$method" = "POST" ] && [ -n "$data" ]; then
    if [ -n "$auth" ]; then
      resp=$(curl -s -w "\n%{http_code}" -m 10 -X POST "$url" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "Authorization: Bearer $auth" -d "$data" 2>/dev/null)
    else
      resp=$(curl -s -w "\n%{http_code}" -m 10 -X POST "$url" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d "$data" 2>/dev/null)
    fi
  else
    if [ -n "$auth" ]; then
      resp=$(curl -s -w "\n%{http_code}" -m 10 "$url" -H "Authorization: Bearer $auth" 2>/dev/null)
    else
      resp=$(curl -s -w "\n%{http_code}" -m 10 "$url" 2>/dev/null)
    fi
  fi
  code=$(echo "$resp" | tail -1)
  body=$(echo "$resp" | sed '$d')

  if [ -n "$expected" ]; then
    if echo "$body" | python3 -c "import sys,json;d=json.load(sys.stdin);exit(0 if $expected else 1)" 2>/dev/null; then
      pass "$name"
    else
      fail "$name — assertion failed"
    fi
  elif [ "$code" = "200" ] || [ "$code" = "201" ]; then
    pass "$name (HTTP $code)"
  else
    fail "$name (HTTP $code)"
  fi
}

# =========================================================================
section "1. BACKEND SERVICE HEALTH (via gateway aggregator)"
# =========================================================================
# F-03 (audit 2026-05-15): rewritten from per-port direct checks to the
# gateway's /health/deep aggregator. The legacy form
# (`http://localhost:6003/health` etc.) tested an older architecture where
# every service was host-port-exposed; in the current docker-compose only
# the nginx gateway, postgres and redis are exposed. The previous form
# returned 22/29 false-failures on a healthy stack.
#
# `/health/deep` is exposed by nginx-gateway → api-gateway, returns
# JSON like {ready, status, checks: {redis, postgres, auth, originate,
# anchoring}}. Each service entry has {status: 'up'|'down', latencyMs}.
DEEP_RESP=$(curl -s -m 10 "$GATEWAY/health/deep" 2>/dev/null) || DEEP_RESP=""
if [ -z "$DEEP_RESP" ]; then
  fail "Gateway /health/deep — unreachable"
else
  # Use python3 (already a hard dep elsewhere in this script) to parse.
  while IFS=$'\t' read -r svc status latency; do
    [ -z "$svc" ] && continue
    if [ "$status" = "up" ]; then
      pass "$svc (latency ${latency}ms)"
    else
      fail "$svc — status=$status"
    fi
  done < <(printf '%s' "$DEEP_RESP" | python3 -c "
import sys, json
try:
    d = json.load(sys.stdin)
    for name, info in (d.get('checks') or {}).items():
        status = info.get('status', '?')
        latency = info.get('latencyMs', '?')
        print(name + '\t' + str(status) + '\t' + str(latency))
except Exception as e:
    sys.stderr.write('parse-error: ' + str(e) + '\n')
")
fi

# =========================================================================
section "2. FRONTEND PORTALS"
# =========================================================================
check_http "Issuer Portal" "$GATEWAY/"
check_http "Verifier Portal" "$GATEWAY/verify/"
check_http "Admin Portal" "$GATEWAY/admin/"
check_http "Status Page" "$GATEWAY/status/"
check_http "Website" "$GATEWAY/website/"
check_http "Showcase" "$GATEWAY/showcase/"

# =========================================================================
section "3. API GATEWAY"
# =========================================================================
check_http "Gateway health" "$GATEWAY/health"
check_http "API root" "$GATEWAY/api/"

if [ "${1:-}" = "--quick" ]; then
  section "QUICK MODE — skipping API tests"
else
  # =========================================================================
  section "4. AUTH API"
  # =========================================================================
  check_api "Login (demo)" "POST" "$GATEWAY/api/auth/login" \
    '{"email":"demo@secuura.io","password":"demo123"}' \
    "d.get('success') and d.get('data',{}).get('accessToken')"

  check_api "Password reject (short)" "POST" "$GATEWAY/api/auth/register" \
    '{"email":"smoke@t.io","password":"abc"}' \
    "not d.get('success')"

  check_api "Forgot password" "POST" "$GATEWAY/api/auth/forgot-password" \
    '{"email":"demo@secuura.io"}' \
    "d.get('success')"

  # Get auth token for protected endpoints
  TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST "$GATEWAY/api/auth/login" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"email":"demo@secuura.io","password":"demo123"}' | \
    python3 -c "import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)['data']['accessToken'])" 2>/dev/null) || TOKEN=""

  if [ -n "$TOKEN" ]; then
    pass "Auth token obtained"
  else
    fail "Auth token — could not obtain"
  fi

  # =========================================================================
  section "5. DOCUMENT API"
  # =========================================================================
  if [ -n "$TOKEN" ]; then
    check_api "List documents" "GET" "$GATEWAY/api/documents" "" \
      "len(d.get('documents',[])) > 0" "$TOKEN"

    # Create a test document with unique hash each run
    SMOKE_HASH=$(python3 -c "import hashlib,time;print('sha256:'+hashlib.sha256(str(time.time()).encode()).hexdigest())" 2>/dev/null)
    DOC_RESP=$(curl -s -X POST "$GATEWAY/api/documents" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
      -d "{\"title\":\"Smoke-Test\",\"type\":\"certificate\",\"contentHash\":\"$SMOKE_HASH\"}" 2>/dev/null)
    DOC_ID=$(echo "$DOC_RESP" | python3 -c "import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin).get('id',''))" 2>/dev/null) || DOC_ID=""

    if [ -n "$DOC_ID" ]; then
      pass "Create document ($DOC_ID)"
    else
      fail "Create document"
    fi

    # Verify document gets anchored (auto-anchor fires on creation in dev mode)
    if [ -n "$DOC_ID" ]; then
      sleep 2  # allow async auto-anchor to complete
      DOC_STATUS=$(curl -s "$GATEWAY/api/documents/$DOC_ID" \
        -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" 2>/dev/null)
      if echo "$DOC_STATUS" | python3 -c "import sys,json;d=json.load(sys.stdin);exit(0 if d.get('status')=='anchored' or d.get('error','')=='Document is already anchored' else 1)" 2>/dev/null; then
        SIMULATED=$(echo "$DOC_STATUS" | python3 -c "import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin).get('blockchain',{}).get('simulated',False))" 2>/dev/null)
        pass "Anchor document (auto-anchored, simulated=$SIMULATED)"
      else
        # Try explicit anchor as fallback
        ANCHOR_RESP=$(curl -s -X POST "$GATEWAY/api/documents/$DOC_ID/anchor" \
          -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
          -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" 2>/dev/null)
        if echo "$ANCHOR_RESP" | python3 -c "import sys,json;d=json.load(sys.stdin);exit(0 if d.get('status')=='anchored' or 'already anchored' in d.get('error','') else 1)" 2>/dev/null; then
          pass "Anchor document (explicit anchor)"
        else
          fail "Anchor document"
        fi
      fi
    fi

    # Verify document
    check_api "Verify document" "POST" "$GATEWAY/api/verification/verify" \
      "{\"documentId\":\"doc-demo-degree-001\"}" \
      "d.get('verified')==True"
  else
    warn "Skipping document tests (no auth token)"
  fi

  # =========================================================================
  section "6. ADMIN API (Dev Mode)"
  # =========================================================================
  check_api "Admin doc-types" "GET" "$GATEWAY/originate/api/admin/document-types" "" \
    "d.get('success') and len(d.get('documentTypes',[])) > 0"
  check_api "Admin workflows" "GET" "$GATEWAY/originate/api/admin/workflows" "" \
    "d.get('success') and len(d.get('workflows',[])) > 0"
  check_api "Admin integrations" "GET" "$GATEWAY/originate/api/admin/integrations" "" \
    "d.get('success')"
  check_api "Admin settings" "GET" "$GATEWAY/originate/api/admin/settings" "" \
    "d.get('success')"
  check_api "Admin verification queue" "GET" "$GATEWAY/originate/api/admin/verification-queue" "" \
    "d.get('success')"
  check_http "System errors stats" "$GATEWAY/originate/api/system-errors/stats"
  # GDPR routes require authentication (security hardening)
  if [ -n "$TOKEN" ]; then
    GDPR_RET=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -m 5 "$GATEWAY/originate/api/gdpr/retention" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" 2>/dev/null)
    if [ "$GDPR_RET" = "200" ]; then pass "GDPR retention (HTTP $GDPR_RET)"; else fail "GDPR retention — expected HTTP 200, got $GDPR_RET"; fi
    GDPR_DSR=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -m 5 "$GATEWAY/originate/api/gdpr/dsr/pending" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" 2>/dev/null)
    if [ "$GDPR_DSR" = "200" ]; then pass "GDPR DSR pending (HTTP $GDPR_DSR)"; else fail "GDPR DSR pending — expected HTTP 200, got $GDPR_DSR"; fi
  else
    warn "GDPR endpoints — skipped (no auth token)"
  fi

  # =========================================================================
  section "7. INTEGRATION SERVICES"
  # =========================================================================
  TS_UUID=$(python3 -c "import uuid;print(str(uuid.uuid4()))" 2>/dev/null || echo "00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000099")
  TS_HASH=$(python3 -c "import hashlib,time;print(hashlib.sha256(str(time.time()).encode()).hexdigest())" 2>/dev/null)
  check_api "Timestamping (create)" "POST" "http://localhost:6004/api/timestamps" \
    "{\"hash\":\"$TS_HASH\",\"timestampType\":\"rfc3161\",\"documentId\":\"$TS_UUID\"}" \
    "d.get('success')"

  check_api "M365 (init)" "POST" "http://localhost:6013/api/connections/init" \
    '{"tenantId":"smoke-test","connectionName":"Smoke","organizationId":"00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001"}' \
    "d.get('success')"

  check_api "VC issue" "POST" "http://localhost:6014/api/credentials" \
    '{"documentId":"smoke-001","documentHash":"sha256:abcd","documentType":"DocumentCertification","documentTitle":"Smoke","issuerId":"i1","issuerName":"Smoke","subjectDid":"did:example:s","subjectName":"S"}' \
    "d.get('success') and d.get('credential',{}).get('@context')"

  # =========================================================================
  section "8. DATABASE PERSISTENCE"
  # =========================================================================
  # Verify the admin tables have data (proves DB init scripts ran)
  DB_TYPES=$(curl -s "http://localhost:6000/api/admin/document-types" 2>/dev/null)
  DB_COUNT=$(echo "$DB_TYPES" | python3 -c "import sys,json;print(len(json.load(sys.stdin).get('documentTypes',[])))" 2>/dev/null) || DB_COUNT=0
  if [ "$DB_COUNT" -gt 0 ]; then
    pass "DB persistence — document_type_configs ($DB_COUNT rows)"
  else
    fail "DB persistence — document_type_configs table empty or unreachable"
  fi

  DB_WORKFLOWS=$(curl -s "http://localhost:6000/api/admin/workflows" 2>/dev/null)
  DB_WF_COUNT=$(echo "$DB_WORKFLOWS" | python3 -c "import sys,json;print(len(json.load(sys.stdin).get('workflows',[])))" 2>/dev/null) || DB_WF_COUNT=0
  if [ "$DB_WF_COUNT" -gt 0 ]; then
    pass "DB persistence — workflow_configs ($DB_WF_COUNT rows)"
  else
    fail "DB persistence — workflow_configs table empty or unreachable"
  fi

  # Verify auth tables (password reset, sessions)
  AUTH_HEALTH=$(curl -s "http://localhost:6003/health" 2>/dev/null)
  AUTH_DB=$(echo "$AUTH_HEALTH" | python3 -c "import sys,json;d=json.load(sys.stdin);print(d.get('database','unknown'))" 2>/dev/null) || AUTH_DB="unknown"
  if [ "$AUTH_DB" = "connected" ] || [ "$AUTH_DB" = "healthy" ]; then
    pass "DB persistence — auth service database connected"
  else
    warn "DB persistence — auth service database: $AUTH_DB"
  fi

  # =========================================================================
  section "9. MULTI-TENANCY & MCP SERVICES"
  # =========================================================================

  # Tokenisation service
  check_health "Tokenisation health" "http://localhost:6021/health"

  TOKENISE_RESP=$(curl -s -X POST "http://localhost:6021/api/tokenise" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"tenantId":"smoke-test","data":{"name":"Smoke User","email":"smoke@test.io"},"fields":["name","email"],"key":"c29tZS10ZXN0LWtleS0zMi1ieXRlcy0xMjM0NQ=="}' 2>/dev/null)
  if echo "$TOKENISE_RESP" | python3 -c "import sys,json;d=json.load(sys.stdin);exit(0 if d.get('success') or 'tokenised' in str(d) else 1)" 2>/dev/null; then
    pass "Tokenisation — tokenise endpoint responds"
  else
    warn "Tokenisation — tokenise endpoint returned unexpected response"
  fi

  # Tenant provisioning
  check_health "Tenant Provisioning health" "http://localhost:6022/health"

  TENANT_LIST=$(curl -s "http://localhost:6022/api/tenants" 2>/dev/null)
  if echo "$TENANT_LIST" | python3 -c "import sys,json;d=json.load(sys.stdin);exit(0 if isinstance(d,list) or d.get('success') else 1)" 2>/dev/null; then
    pass "Tenant Provisioning — list tenants responds"
  else
    warn "Tenant Provisioning — list tenants returned unexpected response"
  fi

  # MCP Server
  check_health "MCP Server health" "http://localhost:6023/health"

  MCP_HASH=$(curl -s -X POST "http://localhost:6023/api/hash" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"content":"smoke-test-content"}' 2>/dev/null)
  if echo "$MCP_HASH" | python3 -c "import sys,json;d=json.load(sys.stdin);exit(0 if d.get('hash') or d.get('success') else 1)" 2>/dev/null; then
    pass "MCP Server — hash endpoint works"
  else
    warn "MCP Server — hash endpoint returned unexpected response"
  fi

  # Platform API (requires admin token)
  ADMIN_TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST "$GATEWAY/api/auth/login" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"email":"admin@secuura.com","password":"admin123"}' | \
    python3 -c "import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)['data']['accessToken'])" 2>/dev/null) || ADMIN_TOKEN=""

  if [ -n "$ADMIN_TOKEN" ]; then
    TENANT_API=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -m 5 \
      "$GATEWAY/api/platform/tenants" \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" 2>/dev/null) || TENANT_API="000"
    if [ "$TENANT_API" = "200" ]; then
      pass "Platform API — /api/platform/tenants (HTTP $TENANT_API)"
    else
      fail "Platform API — /api/platform/tenants (HTTP $TENANT_API)"
    fi
  else
    warn "Platform API — skipped (no admin token)"
  fi

  # =========================================================================
  section "10. STRUCTURED LOGGING"
  # =========================================================================
  SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
  # Verify services produce structured JSON logs (spot-check originate)
  LOG_LINE=$(docker compose -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/docker-compose.yml" logs originate 2>/dev/null | grep '"level"' | head -1) || LOG_LINE=""
  if [ -n "$LOG_LINE" ]; then
    pass "Structured logging — originate produces JSON logs"
  else
    warn "Structured logging — could not verify originate JSON logs"
  fi

  # Verify dev-default warnings appear
  JWT_WARN=$(docker compose -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/docker-compose.yml" logs originate 2>/dev/null | grep -c "development default") || JWT_WARN=0
  if [ "$JWT_WARN" -gt 0 ]; then
    pass "Env validation — dev-default warnings present"
  else
    warn "Env validation — no dev-default warnings found"
  fi

  # =========================================================================
  section "11. REDIS CONNECTIVITY"
  # =========================================================================
  REDIS_OK=$(docker exec secuura-redis redis-cli -a secuura_redis_dev ping 2>/dev/null) || REDIS_OK=""
  if [ "$REDIS_OK" = "PONG" ]; then
    pass "Redis — authenticated connection (PONG)"
  else
    fail "Redis — authentication failed or unreachable"
  fi
fi

# =========================================================================
section "RESULTS"
# =========================================================================
TOTAL=$((PASS + FAIL))
printf "\n  ${GREEN}Passed: $PASS${NC}  ${RED}Failed: $FAIL${NC}  ${YELLOW}Warnings: $WARN${NC}  Total: $TOTAL\n"

if [ $FAIL -gt 0 ]; then
  printf "\n  ${RED}FAILURES:${NC}\n"
  for f in "${FAILURES[@]}"; do
    printf "    ${RED}✗${NC} %s\n" "$f"
  done
  printf "\n"
  exit 1
else
  printf "\n  ${GREEN}All checks passed.${NC}\n\n"
  exit 0
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# TESTS for scripts/stack_guard.sh (KS-666)
# =============================================================================
# The repo has no bats harness, so this is a self-contained runner: plain bash,
# no dependencies, no network, no Docker daemon.
#
# `docker` is stubbed onto PATH so the guard's decisions can be driven
# deterministically — a real daemon would make these tests depend on whatever
# happened to be running on the host, which for a test ABOUT shared-host
# collisions would be self-defeating.
#
# Each case is red before the corresponding guard logic exists and green after;
# to see a case fail, break the matching branch in stack_guard.sh and re-run.
#
# Usage: bash Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/stack_guard.test.sh
# =============================================================================

set -uo pipefail

# GUARD is overridable so a fix can be demonstrated red-then-green against an
# earlier revision of the script, e.g.
#   git show <sha>:Blockchain/Dev/scripts/stack_guard.sh > /tmp/old_guard.sh
#   GUARD=/tmp/old_guard.sh bash .../stack_guard.test.sh
GUARD="${GUARD:-$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)/stack_guard.sh}"
PASS=0
FAIL=0

# --- harness ---------------------------------------------------------------

# Build a throwaway PATH whose `docker` reports exactly the stacks a case wants.
#
# STACKS is a newline-separated table of
#   project|owner|branch|commit|started_at
# so a case can model more than one stack running at once — which is the whole
# point once stack slots exist. The stub honours the
# `--filter label=com.docker.compose.project=X` argument, because the guard's
# correctness now depends on that filter being applied (KS-666: an unscoped
# lookup reads whichever stack started last, not the one being destroyed).
make_docker_stub() {
  local bindir="$1" stacks="$2" count="${3:-0}"
  mkdir -p "$bindir"
  # Trailing newline is REQUIRED: `while read` drops a final unterminated line, so
  # `printf '%s'` here silently deleted the last stack in the table — which for a
  # one-stack case meant the stub reported no stack at all and the guard was
  # being tested against an empty world.
  printf '%s\n' "$stacks" >"$bindir/.stacks"
  cat >"$bindir/docker" <<'STUB'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Model only the shapes stack_guard.sh actually calls.
stacks_file="$(dirname "$0")/.stacks"
count_file="$(dirname "$0")/.count"
want_project=""
for a in "$@"; do
  case "$a" in
    label=com.docker.compose.project=*) want_project="${a#label=com.docker.compose.project=}" ;;
  esac
done
if [[ "$*" == *"--quiet"* ]]; then
  n=$(cat "$count_file" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
  for ((i=1;i<=n;i++)); do echo "container$i"; done
  exit 0
fi
while IFS='|' read -r project owner branch commit started; do
  [[ -n "$project" ]] || continue
  if [[ "$*" == *"com.secuura.stack.commit"* ]]; then
    # Four-field ownership read — scoped to one project.
    [[ -n "$want_project" && "$project" != "$want_project" ]] && continue
    printf '%s|%s|%s|%s\n' "$owner" "$branch" "$commit" "$started"
  else
    # Three-field survey of every stack on the host.
    printf '%s|%s|%s\n' "$project" "$owner" "$branch"
  fi
done <"$stacks_file"
exit 0
STUB
  printf '%s' "$count" >"$bindir/.count"
  chmod +x "$bindir/docker"
}

# A git repo with one commit, so HEAD exists and the tree is clean.
make_repo() {
  local dir="$1"
  mkdir -p "$dir"
  git -C "$dir" init -q
  git -C "$dir" config user.email test@example.com
  git -C "$dir" config user.name test
  echo original >"$dir/tracked.txt"
  git -C "$dir" add tracked.txt
  git -C "$dir" commit -qm initial
}

# Run the guard and assert on its exit code and (optionally) its stderr.
# Args: description, expected_exit, expected_stderr_substring (may be ""),
#       labels, container_count, dirty(yes/no), user, extra guard args...
# KS-691: `expect` is ALSO /usr/bin/expect. A suite that does not define it as a
# shell function does not fail — it silently shells out to the binary, which
# exits 0 having compared nothing, and the suite still reports every case green.
# That happened here: two new cases written as `expect ...` ran the system binary
# and the suite printed "22 passed, 0 failed" while measuring nothing. Defining
# it removes the trap for anyone reaching for the obvious name, and the guard
# below fails loudly if it is ever shadowed back to the binary.
expect() {
  local desc="$1" want="$2" got="$3"
  if [[ "$got" == "$want" ]]; then
    PASS=$((PASS + 1)); printf 'ok   %s\n' "$desc"
  else
    FAIL=$((FAIL + 1)); printf 'FAIL %s\n       want "%s", got "%s"\n' "$desc" "$want" "$got"
  fi
}
expect_val() { expect "$@"; }   # historical alias; same semantics

# Self-guard: prove the comparator is OURS before any case relies on it.
if [[ "$(type -t expect)" != "function" ]]; then
  printf 'FATAL: expect is not a shell function (resolves to %s) — every case below would pass vacuously.\n' \
    "$(command -v expect)" >&2
  exit 2
fi

check() {
  local desc="$1" want_exit="$2" want_msg="$3" labels="$4" count="$5" dirty="$6" as_user="$7"
  shift 7

  local tmp; tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
  make_repo "$tmp/repo"
  make_docker_stub "$tmp/bin" "$labels" "$count"
  if [[ "$dirty" == "yes" ]]; then echo modified >"$tmp/repo/tracked.txt"; fi

  local out got
  out="$(PATH="$tmp/bin:$PATH" REPO_ROOT="$tmp/repo" USER="$as_user" SUDO_USER="$as_user" \
        STACK_PROJECT="${STACK_PROJECT_UNDER_TEST:-mine}" \
        bash "$GUARD" "$@" 2>&1)"
  got=$?

  local ok=1
  [[ "$got" == "$want_exit" ]] || ok=0
  if [[ -n "$want_msg" && "$out" != *"$want_msg"* ]]; then ok=0; fi

  if (( ok == 1 )); then
    PASS=$((PASS + 1)); printf 'ok   %s\n' "$desc"
  else
    FAIL=$((FAIL + 1))
    printf 'FAIL %s\n' "$desc"
    printf '       expected exit %s%s, got exit %s\n' \
      "$want_exit" "${want_msg:+ and stderr containing \"$want_msg\"}" "$got"
    printf '       --- actual output ---\n%s\n       ---------------------\n' "$out"
  fi
  rm -rf "$tmp"
}

# --- cases -----------------------------------------------------------------
# Format: desc  exit  msg  labels  count  dirty  user  [args...]

# The safe baseline: proceeding must stay frictionless, or the guard becomes
# something people route around.
check "clean tree, no stack running -> allowed" \
  0 "" "" 0 no alice

check "clean tree, stack owned by me -> allowed" \
  0 "" "mine|alice|feature/x|abc1234|2026-08-19T10:00:00Z" 35 no alice

# The incident this ticket exists for.
check "foreign-owned stack -> blocked" \
  1 "BLOCKED: this stack belongs to 'bob'" \
  "mine|bob|feature/ks-256-add-openapi|92feea4a9|2026-08-19T09:59:00Z" 35 no alice

check "foreign-owned stack -> reports owner, branch, commit and container count" \
  1 "containers : 35" \
  "mine|bob|feature/ks-256-add-openapi|92feea4a9|2026-08-19T09:59:00Z" 35 no alice

# Uncommitted work is the unrecoverable half — there is no git object to restore.
check "dirty tree, no stack -> blocked" \
  1 "BLOCKED: uncommitted changes" "" 0 yes alice

check "dirty tree names the offending file" \
  1 "tracked.txt" "" 0 yes alice

# Override: available, but explicit.
check "foreign-owned stack + override -> allowed" \
  0 "Override accepted by 'alice'" \
  "mine|bob|feature/x|abc1234|2026-08-19T09:59:00Z" 35 no alice \
  --i-have-confirmed-with-the-owner

check "dirty tree + override -> allowed" \
  0 "Override accepted" "" 0 yes alice \
  --i-have-confirmed-with-the-owner

# A stack started by a bare `docker compose up` has no owner. Blocking on that
# would fire constantly and train the guard out, so it warns instead.
check "unowned stack (owner=unknown), clean tree -> allowed with a notice" \
  0 "records no owner" \
  "mine|unknown|unknown|unknown|unknown" 35 no alice

check "unowned stack + dirty tree -> still blocked on the tree" \
  1 "BLOCKED: uncommitted changes" \
  "mine|unknown|unknown|unknown|unknown" 35 yes alice

# Usage errors are exit 2, distinct from a refusal, so callers can tell a
# misinvocation from a legitimate block.
check "unknown argument -> exit 2" \
  2 "unknown argument" "" 0 no alice --force

check "--help -> exit 0" \
  0 "Usage:" "" 0 no alice --help

# --- stack-slot scoping (KS-666 phase 3) --------------------------------------
# `docker ps` returns newest-first. Before the project filter, a guard invoked in
# slot 2 read whichever stack had started most recently — so it could refuse (or
# permit) based on a DIFFERENT stack's owner and branch than the one about to be
# destroyed. Found running two slots concurrently on the VM.

# Ours is second in ps order, a foreign stack is first: the guard must still read
# OURS. Unscoped, this reads 'bob' and blocks on the wrong stack's facts.
check "two stacks up -> reads OUR project, not the newest" \
  0 "branch     : feature/mine" \
  "theirs|bob|feature/theirs|dead1234|2026-08-19T11:00:00Z
mine|alice|feature/mine|abc1234|2026-08-19T10:00:00Z" 33 no alice

# The mirror case: our own stack is foreign-owned and must still block, even
# though another project's stack is listed first.
check "two stacks up -> blocks on OUR project's owner" \
  1 "BLOCKED: this stack belongs to 'carol'" \
  "theirs|alice|feature/theirs|dead1234|2026-08-19T11:00:00Z
mine|carol|feature/mine|abc1234|2026-08-19T10:00:00Z" 33 no alice

# A stack in another project is not at risk from this operation, so it must be
# reported for awareness but must NOT block.
check "other project's stack is reported but does not block" \
  0 "theirs — owner bob" \
  "theirs|bob|feature/theirs|dead1234|2026-08-19T11:00:00Z
mine|alice|feature/mine|abc1234|2026-08-19T10:00:00Z" 33 no alice

# Our project has nothing running; another project does. Destroying ours cannot
# touch theirs, so this must be allowed.
check "our project down, another project up -> allowed" \
  0 "" \
  "theirs|bob|feature/theirs|dead1234|2026-08-19T11:00:00Z" 0 no alice

# --- unlabelled stacks (KS-666, found in review by @kksecura) ---------------
# An empty label read means EITHER nothing is running OR a stack is running that predates KS-666
# labelling. Before this, both produced byte-identical output — nothing, exit 0 — so the guard
# could not tell a fully-occupied host from an empty one. On merge day EVERY stack is unlabelled,
# so that is precisely when it was blind. Warn (never block): blocking on every pre-existing stack
# is how a guard gets overridden reflexively, the same reasoning as owner='unknown' above.
check "unlabelled stack with containers -> warns and names the count" \
      0 "32 container(s) are running" "" 32 no alice
check "unlabelled stack warning explains it predates KS-666" \
      0 "started before KS-666" "" 32 no alice
check "unlabelled stack warning does NOT block" \
      0 "" "" 32 no alice
check "genuinely empty host stays silent — no false alarm" \
      0 "" "" 0 alice_no_dirty alice
check "unlabelled + dirty tree still blocks on the tree" \
      1 "uncommitted changes" "" 32 yes alice

# --- docker absent ---------------------------------------------------------
# Exit 2, not 0: if we cannot tell whether a stack is running, we must not
# report "safe to proceed".
run_without_docker() {
  local tmp; tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
  make_repo "$tmp/repo"
  mkdir -p "$tmp/emptybin"
  # Resolve bash BEFORE emptying PATH, and invoke it by absolute path: with PATH
  # reduced to an empty directory the interpreter itself is unreachable, and the
  # case exits 127 without ever reaching the guard. The guard checks for docker
  # before it touches git, so an absolute bash is the only tool this case needs.
  local bash_bin; bash_bin="$(command -v bash)"
  local out got
  out="$(PATH="$tmp/emptybin" REPO_ROOT="$tmp/repo" USER=alice \
        "$bash_bin" "$GUARD" 2>&1)"; got=$?
  if [[ "$got" == 2 && "$out" == *"docker is not available"* ]]; then
    PASS=$((PASS + 1)); echo "ok   docker unavailable -> exit 2, not a false all-clear"
  else
    FAIL=$((FAIL + 1))
    echo "FAIL docker unavailable -> exit 2, not a false all-clear (got $got: $out)"
  fi
  rm -rf "$tmp"
}
run_without_docker

# --- summary ---------------------------------------------------------------
# --- KS-691: one line per STACK, not one per container ----------------------
# list_other_stacks reads `docker ps`, which emits a row per labelled CONTAINER.
# Every container in a platform-k stack carries the owner labels, so a single
# foreign stack printed its "NOT affected by this operation" line 33 times —
# measured 2026-09-01 during a real rebuild. Noise on a notice people are meant
# to read is how a notice stops being read. `sort -u` in list_other_stacks.
# This case feeds FOUR containers of one foreign stack and requires exactly one
# line; the control below proves the counter can see more than one when the
# stacks genuinely differ.
count_other_lines() {
  local labels="$1"
  local tmp; tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
  make_repo "$tmp/repo"
  make_docker_stub "$tmp/bin" "$labels" 33
  local out
  out="$(PATH="$tmp/bin:$PATH" REPO_ROOT="$tmp/repo" USER=alice SUDO_USER=alice \
        STACK_PROJECT=mine bash "$GUARD" 2>&1)"
  rm -rf "$tmp"
  printf '%s' "$out" | grep -c ' — owner '
}

expect_val "one foreign stack with 4 containers is listed ONCE" "1" \
  "$(count_other_lines "theirs|bob|feature/theirs|dead1234|2026-08-19T11:00:00Z
theirs|bob|feature/theirs|dead1234|2026-08-19T11:00:00Z
theirs|bob|feature/theirs|dead1234|2026-08-19T11:00:00Z
theirs|bob|feature/theirs|dead1234|2026-08-19T11:00:00Z
mine|alice|feature/mine|abc1234|2026-08-19T10:00:00Z")"

# Control: the counter is not simply always 1 — three DISTINCT foreign stacks
# must still produce three lines, so deduping cannot hide a real neighbour.
expect_val "three distinct foreign stacks are listed three times" "3" \
  "$(count_other_lines "s2|bob|feature/b|dead1|2026-08-19T11:00:00Z
s3|carol|feature/c|dead2|2026-08-19T11:00:00Z
s4|dave|feature/d|dead3|2026-08-19T11:00:00Z
mine|alice|feature/mine|abc1234|2026-08-19T10:00:00Z")"

echo ""
echo "stack_guard: ${PASS} passed, ${FAIL} failed"
(( FAIL == 0 ))
